# soapysdr-module-audio

**SoapySDR driver module for sound-card SDRs and Airspy HF hardware**

- **Version recorded:** 0.1.1
- **Categories:** `hardware`, `sdr`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/pothosware/SoapyAudio/wiki>

## What it does

Presents an ordinary audio input as a SoapySDR device, so a receiver whose IQ output is a stereo pair on a sound card can be used by SoapySDR software. The module also carries support for hardware that pairs an audio IQ path with USB tuning control.

## Why you would want it

A large family of homebrew and kit receivers -- the SoftRock line and its descendants -- produce quadrature audio and nothing else. Without this they are invisible to modern SDR software; with it they behave like any other device.

## Before it will work

A sound card capable of stereo input at the sample rate the receiver needs, and correct channel assignment: swapped I and Q mirrors the spectrum, which is a real and confusing failure.

## How it installs

- apt: `soapysdr-module-audio`

## Known problems

Sound-card SDRs have no way to report their tuning frequency, so the software cannot know where it is listening -- that offset is configuration, not discovery. Consumer sound cards clip and roll off at the edges of their range, so the usable bandwidth is narrower than the sample rate suggests.
